hinweis: Reaction and convergence times of mentions markets after the content drop; exclusions listed separately. Medians are published per resolved outcome because YES and NO cases measure different mechanisms: a YES market reacts to an utterance that happened, a NO market decays as the remaining window empties. Method, data basis and caveats are in `quelle`.

quelle.methode: t0 is the start of the transmission (the content drop); price series at fidelity=1 (minute grid). First reaction = first move of at least 2 cents after t0. Convergence = the price durably settled on the outcome that later resolved. Tradeable window = hours after t0 in which that outcome was still priced below certainty, measured on the price series independently of the 2-cent threshold — it can start before the first reaction (jre_vance_2221: window 0.08 h against a reaction-to-convergence span of 0.03 h) and is not convergence minus reaction.
quelle.datengrundlage: 12 curated status-ok cases plus one documented exclusion from the thesis file data/results/mentions_latency.csv. The raw file with per-case t0 stamps, market ids and price series is not published, so the per-case figures cannot be recomputed from this payload alone. The Mentions example in kategorie_karte.json (median 0.2 / 260.7 min) is the median of exactly these 12 cases.
einschraenkungen: Convergence contains the time until the resolution-relevant statement inside the broadcast: a word said in minute 90 makes convergence at least 90 minutes without the market being slow. Every convergence figure is an upper bound on reaction speed, not a reaction time.

YES and NO cases measure different mechanisms. YES reacts to an utterance that happened (median first reaction 0.1 min). A NO market has no triggering event: its first 2-cent move (median 4.0 min) is drift, and it can only converge once the broadcast is (almost) over. The pooled medians mix both; compare per outcome.
The 2-cent threshold has no placebo baseline: how often a 2-cent move occurs in a quiet window of comparable books was not counter-tested, so in thin books a 'first reaction' can be noise.
n = 12 hand-picked events, not a random sample; selection favours broadcasts with a clean, documentable drop timestamp.
fidelity=1: values of 0.0 and 0.1 minutes sit at the measurement resolution.
Frozen snapshot of 2026-08-07, curated by hand — no generator script exists in the repo, and mentions events keep happening weekly. Nothing after that date is measured.
No per-case t0, market slug or price series is published here; external readers cannot re-derive these rows.
